public_rationale: On March 21, 2025, TechCrunch reported that Meta shared revenue from Llama hosting, citing a plaintiffs' court filing [e1]. The report does not establish revenue actually earned during January–March 2025 on an identified accounting basis [e1]. It therefore establishes neither zero nor positive direct generative-AI revenue for the target quarter [e1].
limitations: Reported revenue-sharing arrangements do not establish when revenue was earned or recognized [e1].
The claim supplies no accounting basis, and the evidence does not provide a matched quarterly revenue measure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Meta is not making any money from generative AI.

statement.excerpt: Meta is not making any money from generative AI.

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion compares revenue and separately distinguishes profit. I therefore read 'making any money' as earning direct revenue, rather than earning a profit.
Direct revenue includes licensing generative models. General advertising improvements do not establish direct generative-AI revenue.
I use January–March 2025, the latest completed reporting quarter publicly reportable before the post.
The statement identifies no accounting basis or source for Meta's purported zero revenue. Its accounting basis remains unknown.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable evidence establishes zero direct generative-AI revenue throughout the target quarter on an identified accounting basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes positive direct generative-AI revenue in the target quarter on a basis matching the claim.
